With reference to "Residential Uses", the regulations provide that a minimum of 15 square feet of open space will be provided for each 100 square feet of gross floor area. The specific activities proposed for the open space will be determined by the Authority's design advisory group which will take into consideration residents' recreational needs as well as aesthetics in arriving at its determinations.
Archeological Considerations:
with respect to the two known archaeological sites, HUD cannot agree with the Department's recommendation that the final environmental impact statement include "adequately substantiated discussion of the accomplishment" of the evaluation of the two known archaeological sites in the study area. The letter from the State Archaeologist was written in response to the CRA's consultant request that he consider both the project area and the study area. This study area was defined as four community districts within the City of Cambridge. The location of the two archaeological sites are about one-half and about one mile, respectively, from the project area. Project activities will not affect them. HUD believes that a careful reading of the archaeologist's letter will confirm the conclusion that the project appears to have no adverse archaeological impacts. Your attention is directed to DEIS page D-1-2.
Historic Sites and Districts
With respect to historic sites and districts, HUD believes that the treatment presented in the DEIS is sufficient and that the comments and review made by the Massachusetts Historical Commission substantiate the adequacy of that treatment.
U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (July 7, 1977)
HUD acknowledges receipt of the Commission's review and its determination that the proposed action has no significant radiological health and safety impacts and will not adversely affect any activities subject to its regulation.
U.S. Department of Agriculture (July 27, 19?7)
HUD acknowledges receipt of the review of the Department's Soil conservation Service and its statement that it has no comments that are relative to its areas of concern.
